components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one next step on a screen; at most one per view.

components.css: .ds-btn-primary{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;height:32px;padding:0 12px;border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:var(--radius-control,6px);font:500 0.875rem/1 var(--font-body,'Inter Variable',system-ui,sans-serif);white-space:nowrap;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1),color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1);background:var(--color-accent,oklch(52% 0.19 257));color:var(--color-accent-ink,oklch(99.4% 0.003 250));} .ds-btn-primary:hover{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--color-accent,oklch(52% 0.19 257)) 90%,transparent);} .ds-btn-primary:active{background:color-mix(in oklch,var(--color-accent,oklch(52% 0.19 257)) 80%,transparent);} .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--color-focus,oklch(52% 0.19 257));outline-offset:2px;}

components.css: .ds-card{background:var(--color-surface,oklch(99.4% 0.003 250));border:1px solid var(--color-rule,oklch(86.5% 0.009 253));border-radius:var(--radius-card,10px);overflow:hidden;font:400 0.875rem/1.25rem var(--font-body,'Inter Variable',system-ui,sans-serif);color:var(--color-ink,oklch(20% 0.016 260));} .ds-card-head{padding:10px 16px;border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule,oklch(86.5% 0.009 253));font:600 0.875rem/1.25rem var(--font-display,'Space Grotesk Variable',system-ui,sans-serif);letter-spacing:-0.02em;} .ds-rows{margin:0;padding:0 16px;} .ds-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:minmax(6.5rem,11rem) minmax(0,1fr);align-items:center;column-gap:16px;min-height:40px;padding:6px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule,oklch(86.5% 0.009 253));} .ds-row:last-child{border-bottom:0;} .ds-row dt{color:var(--color-ink-3,oklch(53.5% 0.016 256));} .ds-row dd{margin:0;display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:4px 12px;} .ds-mono{font:400 0.75rem/1rem var(--font-mono,'JetBrains Mono Variable',ui-monospace,monospace);} .ds-meta{font-size:0.75rem;color:var(--color-ink-3,oklch(53.5% 0.016 256));} .ds-actions{display:flex;gap:4px;margin-right:-4px;} .ds-ghost{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:6px;height:28px;padding:0 8px;border:0;border-radius:var(--radius-control,6px);background:transparent;color:var(--color-ink-2,oklch(42.5% 0.018 257));font:500 0.75rem/1 inherit;cursor:pointer;} .ds-ghost.ds-icon{width:28px;padding:0;justify-content:center;} .ds-ghost:hover{background:var(--color-surface-2,oklch(94% 0.006 252));color:var(--color-ink,oklch(20% 0.016 260));} .ds-ghost:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--color-focus,oklch(52% 0.19 257));outline-offset:2px;}

narrative.overview:
PRTG-NATS is the control room for a fleet of probes spread over sites the operator cannot see. Its job is the job of a good control room: the state of everything is readable at a glance, and every intervention is deliberate, labelled and confirmed. The interface stays quiet so that the one thing that is wrong can be loud.

Density is that of a working tool, not a showcase. Rows of label and value, machine values in monospace, states as small flat tints, actions at the right edge of the row they belong to. Surfaces are flat and separated by hairlines, not lifted by shadows. One signal blue marks what can be done next; amber and red are reserved for what needs attention. Light and dark are equal citizens, because the same people check the fleet at a desk in the day and on a phone at night.

It is explicitly not a generic AI admin template (no gradients, glows, pill buttons, emoji icons or coloured tile dashboards), not a copy of PRTG's own look, and not playful consumer design (no illustrations, mascots or motion for its own sake).
keyCharacteristics: Flat surfaces, hairline borders, no decorative depth.
One accent, used for the primary action, focus and running work only.
States are text with a tint, never shaped like buttons.
Every machine value - id, address, version, checksum - is monospaced.
Actions sit at the right edge of their row; rare and destructive ones wait in a menu.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue covers under 5% of any screen: one primary action per view, the focus ring, the active state. A second primary button on a screen is a bug - with one exception: the submit button of a form is primary within that form.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red say healthy, attention and fault. They are never used to decorate, to group, or to make a screen look alive.

rules.name: The Equal Night Rule
rules.body: Every surface is designed for light and dark at once; only the semantic aliases flip, the ramps never do.

rules.name: The Machine Value Rule
rules.body: If a machine produced it - an id, an address, a hash, a version - it is set in mono. If a person reads it as language, it is not.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Figures are tabular everywhere, so a column of numbers does not shift by a pixel per row.

rules.name: The One Line Rule
rules.body: A value and its actions share one line where there is room, and wrap together where there is not. They are never spread over the card.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Nothing at rest casts a shadow. Depth appears only for a layer that floats over other content.

dos: Do put a row's actions at its right edge as ghost buttons with a Lucide icon, and move rare or destructive ones into the row's action menu.
Do confirm every destructive or secret-revealing step in a dialog; the solid red button lives only there.
Do keep one primary button per view, and none when nothing is the obvious next step.
Do set every machine value in mono and every figure tabular.
Do design each surface in light and dark at once.
donts: Don't use gradients, glows, pill-shaped buttons, emoji icons or coloured tile dashboards.
Don't imitate PRTG's own visual style; the tool works with PRTG and does not present itself as part of it.
Don't add illustrations, mascots or motion for its own sake.
Don't shape a state like a control: no border, capitals or hover on a badge.
Don't place actions as loose text links beside or under a value.
Don't cast a shadow on anything at rest.
Don't make a badge clickable, or draw a selected filter as a primary button.
Don't use typed glyphs (arrows, check marks) where an icon belongs.
